list_records.description: List DNS records in a zone

export_zone.description: Export a zone as a BIND file

batch.description: Batch delete, patch, put, and post DNS records

list.description: List every zone the connected token can see

list_accounts.description: List Cloudflare accounts the token can see

get_settings.description: Read every setting on a zone. zone_id is 32 lowercase hex.

get_setting.description: Read one zone setting. setting_id is 1 to 64 characters of lowercase letters, digits, and underscores.

update_setting.description: Change one of ssl, always_use_https, security_header, min_tls_version, or automatic_https_rewrites. Reads the setting, PATCHes it, and reads it again. Returns setting_id, before, after, and applied. For ssl, always_use_https, min_tls_version and automatic_https_rewrites, give value: ssl is off, flexible, full, or strict; always_use_https and automatic_https_rewrites are on or off; min_tls_version is 1.0, 1.1, 1.2, or 1.3. For security_header (HSTS), give strict_transport_security instead, an object whose only keys are enabled, max_age, include_subdomains, preload, and nosniff; max_age is an integer from 0 to 31536000 and the rest are booleans; it is sent as { strict_transport_security }. Giving both, or the one the setting does not take, is refused. applied is whether after equals what was sent; for security_header it compares after.strict_transport_security key by key. When the PATCH is accepted and the second read throws or returns success false, after and applied are null and reason is read after write failed.

get_bot_management.description: Read bot management for a zone.

list_certificate_packs.description: List certificate packs for a zone, including every status.

list_workers_routes.description: List Workers routes on a zone.

list_access_apps.description: List Access applications for an account, following page while result_info.total_pages says there are more, at 1000 per page. hostname, when given, keeps applications whose domain, any self_hosted_domains entry, or any destinations uri has a host part matching that hostname; a wildcard is matched generously (each * matches any run of characters, and *.x also covers x), and an application with a destination that has no uri is kept and named in unresolved. The host part is the text before the first slash, lowercased, without a trailing dot. Returns access_enabled true, filtered_by (the hostname, or null), and unresolved. When Cloudflare refuses the first page with 403 and 9999 as its only code, Access is not enabled on the account: the answer is success true, access_enabled false, an empty result and an empty unresolved, a reading that no Access application applies. Any other refusal, including a 403 without that code, with another code beside it, or after a page was read, is a vendor_error.

list_projects.description: List Pages projects in an account

list_deployments.description: List deployments for a Pages project

create_project.description: Create a Pages project. name is lowercase letters, digits, and hyphens, 1 to 58 characters, with no leading or trailing hyphen.

add_domain.description: Attach a domain to a Pages project. This does not create the DNS CNAME record. The domain stays pending until that record exists. The record is Zone Publisher's job.

remove_domain.description: Detach a custom domain from a Pages project. The DNS record is left in place; removing it is Zone Publisher's job.

delete_project.description: Delete a Pages project and every deployment in it. Reads the project first and refuses while any domain other than its own pages.dev subdomain is attached, and when the read carries no domain list; remove_domain comes first. Best effort: a domain attached between the read and the delete is not caught. Cloudflare may refuse a project with many deployments.

deploy.description: Deploy static kit output to Pages production by Direct Upload. Replaces what production serves. dir must be a directory named dist whose parent directory is named site and contains a regular file kit.json, and neither site nor dist may be a symbolic link. Refuses the user-config credential directory, the home directory, a tree whose root contains _worker.js or a functions directory, more than 20000 files, any file over 25 MiB, any file whose upload request alone would exceed 3 MiB (about 2.25 MiB on disk), and a file that changes between hashing and upload. Skips node_modules, hidden names other than .well-known, names shaped like private keys or certificate bundles, .env files, _routes.json, and links that resolve outside dir, and lists every skip in the result. _headers and _redirects are sent with the deployment and are not assets. The upload token rides the proxy as an Authorization header on the asset calls, verified live 2026-09-25. A kit payload may carry the kit's Function from site/dist-function/, the sibling of dir, only when that directory exists. It must be a real directory, not a link, holding exactly the regular files _worker.js, _routes.json, schedule.bin and function.json. Any other entry, including a hidden name, a folder or a link, refuses the deploy before any call. _worker.js is admitted only when its sha256 is listed in kit-function.json beside this connector; a missing or malformed list refuses every such deploy. function.json must name those three files' sha256, the kitVersion of that listed fingerprint and of site/kit.json, and the buildTime string recorded in site/.astro/kit-build.json. _routes.json is version 1 with only include and exclude, at most 100 rules, each starting with / and at most 100 characters. schedule.bin must start with WKS1 and a JSON header whose v is 1; nothing else in it is interpreted. The connector builds the Worker bundle: metadata naming _worker.js as main_module with no bindings, _worker.js as application/javascript+module, and schedule.bin as application/octet-stream. The bundle stays within 2 MiB. The deployment request stays within the same base64 cap as deploy_with_functions, and over that cap the deploy is refused before any call and names how many scheduled instants the Function carries. The four files are re-read before the deployment is created. Nothing under dist-function/ is an asset, and functions-filepath-routing-config.json is not sent. When dist-function/ is absent the deploy is unchanged and the result's function is null; when it is present, function reports the kit version, the fingerprint, the schedule size, the route-rule counts, and what was carried.

bind_d1.description: Bind one D1 database onto a Pages project under one binding name. This can overwrite a binding of the same name. environments names production, preview, or both, and defaults to both when omitted. Duplicates are refused. The patch contains only the named environments and only that binding. collateral_changes lists the names of other settings the patch changed, never their values. A failed bind still reports collateral_changes.

deploy_with_functions.description: Deploy static build output that is not a kit site, plus a Pages Functions bundle, to production by Direct Upload. Runs on the local gateway only. dir and functions_build are absolute paths in the platform's normal form, with no . or .. or repeated separator (on Windows, no /) and no symbolic link anywhere in their spelling. dir is not the home directory, not the credential directory, not the filesystem root, and not a kit payload (a site/dist, any directory whose parent holds kit.json, or any directory inside a kit's dist, which go through cloudflare.pages.deploy). Its root must not contain functions, _worker.js, _worker.bundle, functions-filepath-routing-config.json, package.json, wrangler.toml, wrangler.json, or wrangler.jsonc, in any letter case; _worker.js, _worker.bundle or functions-filepath-routing-config.json anywhere below it stops the deploy, and package.json, package-lock.json or a wrangler config below its root is skipped and listed. functions_build is a separate absolute directory, not inside dir and not containing dir, whose entries are exactly the regular files _worker.bundle, _routes.json, functions-filepath-routing-config.json and build.json. build.json is a JSON object whose assets is dir, whose functions names by its real path a functions source outside dir, and whose sources lists each source file's sha256; a file in dir with a listed source's bytes stops the deploy. It is returned as provenance and never sent. The bundle is at most 2 MiB and must parse strictly as multipart: each part carries only Content-Disposition (form-data, a quoted name and an optional quoted filename equal to it) and Content-Type, each once, and part names are unique and plain ASCII (letters, digits, . _ - /); one metadata part of JSON naming a main_module part, with bindings absent or an empty array; module parts typed as Wrangler types modules. The bundle sent is rebuilt from what was screened. Bindings come from the project through cloudflare.pages.bind_d1, not from the bundle. _routes.json is version 1, include is a non-empty array of strings, exclude is an array of strings, together at most 100 rules, and every rule starts with /. functions-filepath-routing-config.json is a JSON object with a routes array. The deployment request is refused when its base64 length exceeds 3 MiB. A file that changes between screening and creation stops the deploy. The static walk applies the same screens as pages.deploy and lists every skip.

deploy_static.description: Deploy a static build output that is neither a kit payload nor a site with Pages Functions to Pages production by Direct Upload. Runs on the local gateway only, because it reads local files. dir is an absolute path in the platform's normal form, with no . or .. or repeated separator (on Windows, no /) and no symbolic link anywhere in its spelling. It is not the home directory, not the credential directory, and not the filesystem root. A kit payload is refused (a site/dist, any directory whose parent holds kit.json, or any directory inside a kit's dist): use cloudflare.pages.deploy. A declared root is a directory whose AGENTS.md is a regular file, not a link, opening with a line --- and closing that frontmatter with a line --- within the first 64 KiB, with a line between them matching root: or type:, ignoring a leading UTF-8 byte-order mark and allowing leading spaces or tabs on the key. An opening --- with no closing --- inside that scan, when the file is longer than the scan, is refused as unreadable. dir is refused when it is a declared root, and when its parent is one; an AGENTS.md at either place that exists but cannot be read is refused. Higher ancestors are not examined. At the root of dir, in any letter case, AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, .git (file or directory), zArchive, a directory named memory, .env, and any name starting .env. are refused as a working folder. Server code anywhere in dir, in any letter case, is refused: a file named _worker.js, _worker.bundle, or functions-filepath-routing-config.json, or a directory named functions; use cloudflare.pages.deploy_with_functions. package.json, wrangler.toml, wrangler.json, and wrangler.jsonc at the root are refused as not build output. Below the root, AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, .git of any type, zArchive, .env, and a name starting .env. are refused rather than skipped; a directory named memory below the root is walked and uploaded. The walk checks the root for working-folder markers again. A link is refused when any segment of its resolved path is a working-folder marker, and the reason names the link. Each skipped hidden directory and each skipped node_modules is screened by name, not following links, and a walk marker at any depth is refused; more than 20000 entries across those directories is refused as too large to screen, and a directory inside one that cannot be read is refused as could not be screened. The walk skips node_modules, hidden names other than .well-known, names shaped like private keys or certificate bundles, package.json, package-lock.json, and wrangler configs below the root, _routes.json, and links that resolve outside dir or point at a directory, and lists every skip. _headers and _redirects are sent with the deployment and are not assets. Refuses an empty tree, more than 20000 files, any file over 25 MiB, any file whose upload request alone would exceed 3 MiB, a deployment request whose base64 length exceeds 3 MiB, and a file that changes between hashing and upload. The upload token is never returned. A non-empty web_analytics_token anywhere in the result is replaced with [redacted]; null and an empty string are left as they are. The same replacement applies to every pages result except a d1_ action.

list_web_analytics_sites.description: List Cloudflare Web Analytics sites in an account. Reads /rum/site_info/list 100 at a time, at most 50 pages. The list is complete when result_info.total_pages is a number and every page up to it was read, or, when total_pages is absent, when the first page returned fewer than 100 sites. Otherwise the action is vendor_error with reason site listing incomplete and returns no partial list. A page whose success is false or whose result is not an array is a vendor_error. Each site is returned as site_tag, host, auto_install, enabled, zone_tag, zone_name, rule_hosts, and created; a value that is absent is null and rule_hosts is the distinct string hosts of the site's rules. site_token and snippet are never returned.

enable_web_analytics.description: Switch on Cloudflare Web Analytics for a Pages project, attaching the named site or creating one for the project's pages.dev host. The beacon is added to pages served by a deployment made after the switch. The site's token and snippet are never returned. Every pages result except a d1_ action replaces a non-empty web_analytics_token, at any depth, with [redacted]; null and an empty string are left as they are. already_on requires a non-empty web_analytics_tag and a non-empty web_analytics_token; the same site_tag or an omitted site_tag then reports already_on and nothing else is called. A tag with no token is repaired by reading that site and patching, and action is repaired. A different site_tag is refused and names the current site, whether or not the token is present. An unknown site_tag is refused. Creating a site requires the project's subdomain to be a string ending in .pages.dev, and posts exactly { host, auto_install: false }. The project is then patched with exactly build_config.web_analytics_tag and build_config.web_analytics_token. collateral_changes lists the names of other build_config settings the patch changed, and deployment_configs when it differs, never their values. Applied means the patch answer shows the tag sent and a web_analytics_token equal to the token sent. Otherwise the result is analytics not applied, with created_site_tag when this call created the site. A thrown patch re-reads the project: success when the re-read shows the tag and token sent, analytics not applied when the re-read shows them absent, and analytics outcome unknown when the re-read fails. That last reason claims nothing about whether the project sends to a site this call created.

delete_web_analytics_site.description: Delete a Web Analytics site and its history. Refuses while a Pages project in the account names the site in build_config.web_analytics_tag, and names those projects. The check is best effort: projects are read 10 at a time, at most 50 pages, and a project that starts naming the site after the listing is not caught. The listing is complete when result_info.total_pages is a number and every page up to it was read, or, when total_pages is absent, when the first page returned fewer than 10 projects. An incomplete listing or a row that is not an object is vendor_error with reason project listing incomplete and deletes nothing. A failed project listing deletes nothing. An unknown site_tag is refused. The site's token and snippet are never returned.

d1_list_databases.description: List D1 databases in an account. name filters by database name. page, when given, is an integer of 1 or more. per_page, when given, is an integer from 1 to 10000.

d1_create_database.description: Create a D1 database. name is required. primary_location_hint, when given, is one of wnam, enam, weur, eeur, apac, oc.

d1_query.description: Run one read-only D1 query and return the vendor envelope. After leading whitespace, sql must open with SELECT followed by a character that is not a letter, digit, underscore or semicolon, and it may contain no semicolon except an optional one as the last non-whitespace character; the published pattern is that rule. D1 splits statements on semicolons with no regard for string literals, so the semicolon rule is absolute. sql is at most 100000 code points. params, when given, is an array of at most 100 strings. A statement that is not that single SELECT is refused; use cloudflare.pages.d1_execute.

d1_execute.description: Run D1 SQL that is not limited to a single SELECT and return the vendor envelope. sql is at most 100000 code points. params, when given, is an array of at most 100 strings. D1 splits statements on semicolons with no regard for string literals.

d1_apply_migration.description: Read one local .sql file and apply it on the local gateway only. Records a Wrangler-compatible d1_migrations row under the file's basename. A name already recorded is reported already_applied and nothing else runs. D1 splits on semicolons, so a semicolon inside a string literal or a trigger body is split too. Whether a failed statement rolls back earlier ones is D1's and is not promised. A file over 1 MiB (1048576 bytes) is refused; apply it with Wrangler: wrangler d1 migrations apply. The path must be absolute, must not contain a symbolic link, and must not be a credential file.

d1_delete_database.description: Delete a D1 database and the data in it.

list_domains.description: List custom domains on a Pages project.

get_domain.description: Read one Pages custom domain, including its activation status.

retry_domain_validation.description: Ask Pages to validate a custom domain again. PATCH with no body.

delete.description: Delete an empty redirect ruleset, and nothing more. Reads the ruleset first. Refuses unless phase is http_request_dynamic_redirect on zones or http_request_redirect on accounts (invalid_arguments, field ruleset_id, reason not a redirect ruleset, with the phase read). Refuses unless rules is empty or absent (field ruleset_id, reason ruleset not empty, with rule_count). A read that throws propagates and nothing is deleted. A read with success false or no result is vendor_error and nothing is deleted. The empty check is best effort: it uses the read just before the DELETE, and a rule someone else adds in between is deleted with the ruleset.

list.description: List rulesets on an account or a zone, following result_info.cursors.after until it is absent, and return every row in one envelope.

get_phase_entrypoint.description: Read the entrypoint ruleset for any phase in the enum, which is Cloudflare's ruleset phase list. A 404 is exists false with result null, not an error. Any other thrown error propagates. A phase outside the enum is invalid_arguments. Writing a phase stays on put_phase_entrypoint, which accepts only the two redirect phases.

list_page_rules.description: List Page Rules on a zone.

list_list_items.description: List every item in an account filter list, following result_info.cursors.after until it is absent, and return every row in one envelope.

put_phase_entrypoint.description: Replace the entrypoint rules for a redirect phase. phase must be http_request_dynamic_redirect when accounts_or_zones is zones, or http_request_redirect when it is accounts. rules is a non-empty array of at most 100 objects, and each rule action must be redirect. A rule object that has a position key is refused on field rules. expected_version is required: the string none only when no entrypoint exists, or the current version string. none when an entrypoint exists is refused with reason entrypoint exists, current_version, and rule_count. A version that is absent or different is refused with reason version mismatch and current_version. The expected_version check is best effort: it compares against the read taken just before the PUT, a write by anyone else in between is overwritten, and the guard does not make the replace atomic. Otherwise PUT { rules, description }. If that PUT throws a 404 and the entrypoint was absent, POST a ruleset named default with kind zone or root. Returns the envelope plus created_with put or post.

add_rule.description: Add a redirect rule to a ruleset. The rule action must be redirect. A position key on the rule object is refused on field rule. zones requires zone_id and refuses account_id. accounts requires account_id and refuses zone_id. position, when given, is an object with exactly one of before, after, or index. before and after are strings and may be empty. index is an integer of 1 or more. Reads the ruleset first and refuses unless its phase is http_request_dynamic_redirect on zones or http_request_redirect on accounts (invalid_arguments, field ruleset_id, reason not a redirect ruleset, with the phase read). A read that throws propagates. A read with success false or no result is vendor_error and nothing is written.

update_rule.description: Replace a redirect rule. Reads the ruleset first and refuses unless its phase is http_request_dynamic_redirect on zones or http_request_redirect on accounts (field ruleset_id, reason not a redirect ruleset, with the phase read), and unless rule_id is one of rules[].id (field rule_id, reason rule not in ruleset). A read that throws propagates. A read with success false or no result is vendor_error and nothing is written. The PATCH body is the rule. A position key on the rule is refused on field rule. The rule action must be redirect.

reorder_rule.description: Move a rule inside a redirect ruleset. Reads the ruleset first and refuses unless its phase is http_request_dynamic_redirect on zones or http_request_redirect on accounts (field ruleset_id, reason not a redirect ruleset, with the phase read), and unless rule_id is one of rules[].id (field rule_id, reason rule not in ruleset). A read that throws propagates. A read with success false or no result is vendor_error and nothing is written. The PATCH body is { position } only. position has exactly one of before, after, or index. before and after are strings and may be empty. index is an integer of 1 or more.

remove_rule.description: Remove a rule from a redirect ruleset. Reads the ruleset first and refuses unless its phase is http_request_dynamic_redirect on zones or http_request_redirect on accounts (field ruleset_id, reason not a redirect ruleset, with the phase read), and unless rule_id is one of rules[].id (field rule_id, reason rule not in ruleset). A read that throws propagates. A read with success false or no result is vendor_error and nothing is deleted.

create_list.description: Create an account redirect list. kind is always redirect. name is 1 to 50 characters of lowercase letters, digits, and underscores. description, when given, is at most 500 characters.

add_list_items.description: Add redirect items to a list. The POST body is the items array itself. Each item is exactly { redirect: { source_url, target_url, status_code, preserve_query_string, include_subdomains, subpath_matching, preserve_path_suffix } } with source_url and target_url required non-empty strings and the flags optional. status_code, when given, is 301, 302, 307, or 308. From 1 to 1000 items. Returns operation_id and one read of that bulk operation. A thrown status read, or an envelope with success false, keeps operation_id, sets operation to null, and sets operation_read to vendor_error. http_status is copied from the thrown signal, and is null otherwise. A successful envelope with no result sets operation to null.

remove_list_items.description: Remove items from a list. DELETE body is { items: [{ id }, ...] }. item_ids is 1 to 1000 ids of 1 to 64 letters, digits, underscores, or hyphens. Returns operation_id and one read of that bulk operation. A thrown status read, or an envelope with success false, keeps operation_id, sets operation to null, and sets operation_read to vendor_error. http_status is copied from the thrown signal, and is null otherwise. A successful envelope with no result sets operation to null.
